messages:
kiran: quick follow-up from the admission API brainstorm. we still need a concrete contract for telling the scheduler how urgent a request is without creating a big abuse vector. thoughts?
liz: proposal: three priority flavors - soft (score), suppressible (nonce+weight+ttl), guaranteed (manual enterprise only). suppressible can be revoked by scheduler on anomalies.
sam: revoke rules need to be explicit. if we revoke, we should emit a typed event and short backoff so customers see consistent behavior.
maya: suppression triggers: burst shape mismatch, sudden token reuse, error-rate spike. suppressible should carry a nonce and issuance snapshot to aid audit.
kiran: API sketch: admission -> TokenReply { token, ttl_s, soft_score, suppressible: {nonce, weight, expiry_ms}?, guaranteed_flag? } scheduler consumes soft_score always; suppressible honored only if local budget allows.
liz: audit + retention: store nonce issuance with tenant id, sample of request headers, and signature. 90-day retention for tracing abuse.
sam: metrics before rollout: per-tenant suppressible_issued, accepted, revoked, rejected_reason; global suppressible_budget and budget_decay. dashboards for canary.
maya: test plan: unit nonce lifecycle, integration budget decay, canary on Dedicated, adversarial scenarios (nonce replay, many tiny reqs), chaos to simulate scheduler slowness.
ops-bot: ticket created: infra-ops/PRIORITY-SUPPRESSIBLE-METRICS-177002.
kiran: rollout steps: 1) proto + audit schema PR behind flag, 2) admission issues suppressible but scheduler ignores, 3) telemetry + dashboards live, 4) enable honoring in canary 72h, 5) staged enable for paying tiers.
liz: I'll draft proto and audit log format.
sam: I'll stub dashboards and alerts with conservative thresholds.
maya: I'll own the harness and adversarial suites.
kiran: thanks all 12 reconvene after proto PR.
